purpose: Skeleton-first craniofacial/hyoid audit. Finish coverage of the low-confidence fixed/reference head bones and preserve the active TMJ as a mechanically meaningful articulation.

head_landmarks.note: The head has no modelled ears; porion/TMJ are proportional estimates at 60% head length behind the face, 12 mm below the authored eye ring.

current_a003.fixed_bone_representation: Most cranial/facial bones are short proportional reference sticks placed around an estimated cranial centre rather than full bone envelopes.

tmj_breadth_crosscheck.reading: The current estimated TMJ spacing is within roughly 1.4 SD of one adult male 3D-CT sample. It is plausible as a provisional breadth, but the a003 TMJs were estimated because the source mesh has no ears/porion landmark, so they are not freeze-ready.

findings: The head/face portion of a003 is structurally complete in the 206-bone inventory but not anatomically freeze-ready: nearly all cranial/facial bones are schematic proportional reference sticks rather than bone-specific 3D geometry.

The current bilateral TMJ spacing is provisionally plausible against an adult male CT bicondylar corridor, so there is no evidence for a gross mandibular-width failure comparable with the shoulder or foot.

Mandibular control-stick length (~113 mm) is not directly comparable with published mandibular length/ramus measures because it runs from the bilateral-condyle midpoint toward the mental region. Canonical mandibular geometry must instead store both condyles, gonia, ramus, body and symphysis landmarks explicitly.

The hyoid is currently a single ~19 mm reference stick. Adult hyoid anatomy requires a body plus bilateral greater/lesser cornua measurement framework even though the hyoid remains one conventional bone and has no direct osseous articulation.

Cranial vault/base bones are low priority for exercise skinning but still part of the complete reference skeleton; they must be validated with a landmark/envelope model rather than arbitrary stick lengths.
Existing TMJ opening/glide tests remain useful, but must be rerun after canonical condylar positions and mandible geometry are instantiated.

cranium: bilateral zygomatic breadth and mastoid/temporal reference regions
bone-specific cranial/facial envelopes or surface patches attached to the correct conventional bones
sutural adjacency preserved without treating sutures as large-motion joints
mandible: TMJ contact/disc frame separate from the bone envelope
hyoid: soft-tissue suspension reference only; no invented osseous parent joint
ossicles: keep malleus/incus/stapes fixed/reference roles for exercise purposes
replace arbitrary stick dimensions only if the master claims geometric rather than topological anatomical fidelity

acceptance_tests: Left/right condylar centres are distinct and bicondylar breadth lies inside a multi-source adult male corridor or has a stature-specific justification.
Mandibular breadth, ramus/body geometry and gonial angle use matching source definitions.
TMJ opening lowers the incisor/chin and produces anterior-inferior condylar glide after geometry rebuild.
Hyoid remains unparented by any invented osseous articulation while its 3D body/cornua geometry is represented.
All 22 skull bones and six ossicles remain accounted for with correct sutural/articular adjacency.
